findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted variable naming and dead branch; always returns false
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)` (so `enabled` is true when the flag is OFF), then returns false in both the `if enabled` branch and the fallthrough. The function therefore always returns false regardless of the flag, which matches the intent of hard-disabling, but the code is misleading: the variable named `enabled` actually means 'disabled', and the `if` is dead code. When someone later re-enables the feature by changing the final `return false`, the inverted logic would enable SQL expressions exactly when the flag is OFF. Either simplify to `return false` with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264, or fix the naming so the flag check is correct.

findings.title: TablesList is now dead code that logs every SQL expression attempt at Error level with the raw SQL
findings.body: `TablesList` still constructs a DuckDB `json_serialize_sql` command and calls `RunCommands` on the stub `DB`, which unconditionally returns `not implemented`. Every call therefore hits `logger.Error("error serializing sql", ... "sql", rawSQL, "cmd", cmd)` and the rest of the function (`json.Unmarshal`, `tablesFromAST`) is unreachable. Any user who submits a SQL expression (via the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` path, which is not gated by the new reader.go check) will produce an Error-level log containing their user-supplied SQL on every request, generating log noise and potential alert fatigue for operators. Since the feature is intentionally disabled, `NewSQLCommand` should return the 'not implemented' error directly without exercising the stubbed parsing path.

findings.title: No tests cover the disabled SQL path; existing sql parser tests will break
findings.body: The PR replaces the DuckDB backend with stubs and gates `QueryTypeSQL` in `ReadQuery`, but adds no test asserting that a SQL expression query is rejected (both via `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` and via `NewSQLCommand`/`UnmarshalSQLCommand`). For a security fix the regression test is the main guard against the feature being accidentally re-enabled. Additionally, any existing tests in `pkg/expr/sql` exercising `TablesList`/`tablesFromAST` against the real DuckDB output (e.g. a parser test) will now fail since `RunCommands` always errors; those should be updated or removed in this PR.

findings.title: sqlExpressions feature toggle remains documented but no longer does anything
findings.body: `featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions` is still registered and documented as enabling SQL expressions, but after this change enabling it has no effect: `enableSqlExpressions` always returns false and the backing `DB` returns 'not implemented'. Users who enable the toggle will get the error 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' with no indication why. The toggle's description/docs should state that the feature is disabled pending a secure replacement (or the flag should be removed/hidden) to avoid confusion.
